nodes.name: Insoluble nanoparticle formation
nodes.procedure: The HN liquid used in this work was prepared by slowly adding FeSO4 solution (in H2O) into Ni(NO3)2 solution (in isopropanol). For CAPist-L1, 142.5 g Ni(NO3)2·6H2O and 19.5 g FeSO4·7H2O were dissolved in 2,400 ml i-PrOH and 800 ml deionized water, respectively. The above solutions were then mixed under vigorous stirring to form the HN liquid containing insoluble NiFe nanoparticles.

nodes.name: Seed-assisted heterogeneous nucleation
nodes.procedure: A pre-washed NF (20×20 cm) was then totally immersed into the HN liquid at 25 °C for 24 h, followed by washing with deionized water and drying in a vacuum oven at 25 °C for 12 h to generate CAPist-L1.

nodes.name: NiFe-LDH hydrothermal synthesis
nodes.procedure: 0.350 g Ni(NO3)2·6H2O, 0.162 g Fe(NO3)3·9H2O and 0.32 g urea were dissolved in 30 ml deionized water under vigorous stirring, followed by the immersion of a pre-washed NF (1.5×2.0 cm) into the solution and reaction in a Teflon-lined autoclave at 120 °C for 12 h. After washing with deionized water and drying in a vacuum oven at 25 °C for 12 h, the NiFe-LDH was obtained.
nodes.source_text: For NiFe-LDH, 0.350 g Ni(NO3)2·6H2O, 0.162 g Fe(NO3)3·9H2O and 0.32 g urea were dissolved in 30 ml deionized water... reaction in a Teflon-lined autoclave at 120 °C for 12 h.

nodes.name: Ni4Mo/MoO2 hydrothermal synthesis
nodes.procedure: 0.419 g Ni(NO3)2·6H2O and 0.445 g (NH4)6Mo7O24·4H2O were mixed in 30 ml deionized water to form a solution, followed by the immersion of a pre-washed NF (2.5×3.0 cm) into the solution and then the reaction in a Teflon-lined autoclave at 150 °C for 6 h to form a pre-catalyst. After washing with deionized water and drying in a vacuum oven at 25 °C for 12 h, the pre-catalyst was calcinated at 500 °C for 2 h in a H2/Ar (volume ratio of 5:95) atmosphere to obtain the Ni4Mo/MoO2@NF catalyst.

nodes.characterization_summary: HAADF-STEM of insoluble NiFe nanoparticles (precursors) shows average diameter of 1.57 ± 0.49 nm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: High-angle annular dark-field imaging scanning transmission electron microscopy (HAADF-STEM) images demonstrate that the insoluble nanoparticles were widely and evenly distributed, with an average diameter of 1.57 ± 0.49 nm (Fig. 1b and Supplementary Fig. 1).

properties.description: Transmission Electron Microscopy image showing NiFe nanoparticles with red outlines

nodes.characterization_summary: EDX of insoluble nanoparticles showed uniform distribution of Fe, Ni, O and S.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Energy-dispersive X-ray (EDX) results showed the uniform distribution of Fe, Ni, O and S in the nanoparticles (Supplementary Fig. 2).

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP-MS showed Ni/Fe atomic ratio of 3.96 in insoluble nanoparticles and 2.21 in CAPist-L1 catalyst.
nodes.evidence_snippet: ICP-MS results indicated a Ni/Fe atomic ratio of 2.21 in CAPist-L1.

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD patterns for CAPist-L1 consistent with refined Ni2Fe(SO4)0.5(OH)6(H2O)3.85 (PDF#01-077-4367) with small (001) peak at 8.1° due to large SO4^2- ions.
nodes.evidence_snippet: X-ray diffraction (XRD) patterns for the prepared CAPist-L1 were consistent with the refined Ni2Fe(SO4)0.5(OH)6(H2O)3.85 (based on PDF#01-077-4367; Fig. 1d and Supplementary Fig. 5).

nodes.characterization_summary: Raman peak at 980 cm^-1 confirmed presence of SO4^2- in CAPist-L1.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Raman peak at 980 cm^-1 also confirmed the presence of SO4^2- in CAPist-L1 (Supplementary Fig. 7).

nodes.characterization_summary: X-ray absorption near-edge structure spectra of Fe K edge confirmed oxidation state of Fe in CAPist-L1 similar to typical NiFe-LDH.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Both X-ray absorption near-edge structure spectra of the Fe K edge and X-ray photoelectron spectra of Fe 2p confirmed that the oxidation state of Fe in CAPist-L1 was similar to that in a typical NiFe-LDH catalyst (Supplementary Figs. 8a and 9).

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS Fe 2p confirmed oxidation state of Fe similar to NiFe-LDH; larger Fe–O scattering path (1.56 Å) than NiFe-LDH (1.51 Å).
nodes.evidence_snippet: Both X-ray absorption near-edge structure spectra of the Fe K edge and X-ray photoelectron spectra of Fe 2p confirmed that the oxidation state of Fe in CAPist-L1 was similar to that in a typical NiFe-LDH catalyst (Supplementary Figs. 8a and 9).

nodes.characterization_summary: Fourier transform extended X-ray absorption fine structure showed larger Fe–O scattering path for CAPist-L1 (1.56 Å) than NiFe-LDH (1.51 Å), similar Fe–O–Fe/Ni paths (2.75 Å).
nodes.evidence_snippet: Fourier transform extended X-ray absorption fine structure data showed a larger Fe–O scattering path for CAPist-L1 (1.56 Å) than that for NiFe-LDH (1.51 Å), while their Fe–O–Fe/Ni scattering paths were similar to each other (2.75 Å) (Supplementary Fig. 8b).

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM showed micrometre-scale hydrangea-shaped structures vertically and evenly distributed on honeycomb-like catalyst base for CAPist-L1.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) of CAPist-L1 showed that micrometre-scale hydrangea-shaped structures grew vertically and evenly distributed on a honeycomb-like catalyst base (Fig. 1e).

nodes.characterization_summary: EDX-TEM images indicated uniform distribution of Ni, Fe, O and S in CAPist-L1 catalyst structure.
nodes.evidence_snippet: EDX transmission electron microscopy images indicated that Ni, Fe, O and S were uniformly distributed in the catalyst structure (Supplementary Fig. 11).

nodes.characterization_summary: CAPist-L1 showed lower Brunauer–Emmett–Teller (BET) surface area compared with NiFe-LDH.
nodes.evidence_snippet: various electrochemical measurements confirmed the higher electrochemical surface area (ECSA) of CAPist-L1, which favours higher OER activity even though it showed a lower Brunauer–Emmett–Teller (BET) surface area compared with NiFe-LDH (Supplementary Fig. 16).

nodes.characterization_summary: Nano-scratch measurements determined critical binding force of CAPist-L1 as 65.4 ± 6.0 mN.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Nano-scratch measurements were employed to determine the critical binding force of CAPist-L1, and the obtained value of 65.4 ± 6.0 mN was higher than that of NiFe-LDH (35.2 ± 8.2 mN) (Supplementary Fig. 23).
